newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares under heavy selling pressure.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares under heavy selling pressure.

text.p: Shares of leading Nigerian companies fell again in Wednesday trade but the falls were moderate compared to Tuesday's sharp drop.
The all-share index closed at 8157.89 from 8172.05 on Tuesday.
"Oversupply further helped prices of blue chips down today but it was a far cry from what happened on Tuesday," one trader said..
Besides the general economic depression, Tuesday's fall was attributed to brokers' attempt to curb the activities of unregistered jobbers -- believed to be discounting shares.
PZ Industries closed 20 kobo down at 24.40 naira on Wednesday. Nigerian Breweries was down 20 kobo at 16.80 naira.
UAC was down 10 kobo at 14.15 naira, Lever Brothers was down six kobo 24.45 naira. Bank UBA fell 15 kobo to 13.20 naira.
Oil marketer Total fell to 54.90 naira, 10 kobo lower, despite reports it has been named government's consultant on downstream oil industry operations.
Cadbury continued to slide, ending 25 kobo down at 33.50 naira, just as Nestle ended at 50.90 naira, down 10 kobo.
ADC Airlines at 3.75 naira lost three kobo following an accident on its Tuesday flight to Calabar when one of the airline's two planes skidded off the runway injuring three people.
Guinness maintained its rally and firmed 20 kobo to 8.60 naira.
Healthcare firm Smithkline Beecham closed 20 kobo stronger on an improved perception at 5.50 naira.

Interest in the insurance sector increased and both AIICO and Prestige were respectively five kobo gainers at 15.05 and 6.30 naira. Crusader notched three kobo to 1.30 naira. -- Lagos newsroom +234 12 263 03 17
